_comment: Direction is the whole point. A human map that RESTATES a machine fact is a
second copy of that fact, and a second copy drifts. The fix is not 'write the
map more carefully' -- it is to stop hand-copying the part a machine already
knows, and let a compiler emit that region.
human map      owns prose, judgement, WHY an entry exists
generated block owns ONLY what a registry already says
The generated block is delimited by markers and is regenerated, never edited.
Prose outside the markers is untouched by the compiler, always.
The compiler never writes a map in place. It emits a candidate and reports
drift; applying it is a separate, deliberate act by whoever owns that map.
This is required, not cautious: these maps have concurrent writers.

note: The end marker deliberately carries no generator tag. A reader looking for
the end of a block should not have to match the generator's exact spelling
-- and if the two spellings ever diverged, an unmatched BEGIN would swallow

bundle.owns: which Skills are composed into the plugin, and at what version

abilities.owns: what abilities exist and what type each one is

topology.owns: which children each declared root may hold, and in what role

_targets_note: TARGETS ARE A MACHINE INSTANCE FACT, and this default table is a known
ownership wart, stated rather than hidden: serveros owns the schema and the
projections, hwz-ops owns which map files exist on THIS machine. Ideally the
table moves to hwz-ops (ops/workspace/environment.yaml or a sibling) and this
file keeps only the schema. It is not moved in this round because hwz-ops has
concurrent writers and a second placement authority is exactly the defect §14
is closing. Override with --targets-file until then; the compiler takes either.
Each target asserts: this map carries this machine fact. That assertion is
what makes MAP_VIEW_UNBOUND possible -- without it, a map with no markers is
indistinguishable from a map that was never supposed to have any.

targets.why: It hand-copies the plugin version (v2.0.1) and member count. Both are machine facts.
It hand-draws the DATA_ROOT child tree that topology-contract.json declares.
Its DATA_ROOT / Workspace controlled-vocabulary sections are the same list again.
